text: Drink one cup (about 240 ml) of water every 15 to 20 minutes while working in heat, even if not thirsty. Do not drink more than about 1.4 litres (6 cups) in an hour.

New workers should work no more than 20% of the usual time in heat on day 1, increasing by no more than 20% each day. Workers returning after a break start at 50% on day 1, 60% on day 2, 80% on day 3 and 100% on day 4.
source: NIOSH Criteria for a Recommended Standard: Occupational Exposure to Heat and Hot Environments (2016-106)

text: Heat stroke is an emergency. Warning signs include confusion, slurred speech, fainting, seizures, and very high body temperature, sometimes with hot dry skin. Call 108, move the person to shade, and cool them with water and fanning while waiting.

Heat exhaustion can cause headache, dizziness, nausea, weakness, thirst and heavy sweating. Stop work, move to a cool shaded place, drink water, and loosen clothing. Get medical help if symptoms get worse or do not improve within an hour.
During heat waves, employers should schedule strenuous outdoor work for cooler times of the day, provide shade and drinking water at work sites, and allow frequent rest breaks.
source: NDMA Guidelines for Preparation of Action Plan: Prevention and Management of Heat Wave (2019)

text: WBGT (Wet Bulb Globe Temperature) combines air temperature, humidity, sunlight and wind into one heat-stress number. It is used by OSHA, NIOSH and many armies for work-rest decisions. A humid day can have a higher WBGT than a hotter dry day.

India's official heatwave declaration uses maximum temperature: at least 40 C in the plains, 37 C on the coast or 30 C in the hills, with a departure of at least 4.5 C above normal (or 45 C and above). Humidity does not trigger it, so a humid day can be dangerous without any heatwave warning.

Invisible Heat's rest minutes per hour (15, 30, 45, or stop work) come from how far the forecast WBGT is above the NIOSH limit for the work type. These bands are this project's own planning rule inspired by NIOSH guidance, not an official standard.
